When they disagree

You will learn

How to triage a disagreement: which of the three is lying, and how to find out.

When spec, simulator and board disagree, one of them is lying and the disagreement itself tells you where to look. If the simulator matches the spec but the board differs, suspect constraints, timing, or the model's assumptions -- pin assignments first, they are the usual liar. The widget is the triage tool for exactly that class: before an edit to a Verilog file, every spec and generator it would touch, so a fix cannot silently wander. Breadth first (what changes?), then depth (why does this one?).

Try it

Make the triage list: for each mismatch direction (spec vs simulator, simulator vs board), name the file you would open before any other, and why.
